venue_now: Not shown in the text: the file is arXiv:2502.12054v2, 26 May 2025, with no venue header (p.1). cited_set_resolution.md lists ACL 2025 (Long Papers), pp. 16593-16615.
what_it_is: A physics problem-solving benchmark of 1,200 problems, 25% knowledge-based and 75% reasoning-based (easy, medium, hard, 25% each), 81% with diagrams (p.1, p.4). Problems come from public college-entrance exams, mock exams and physics olympiads (Gaokao, JEE Advanced, IPhO and others), parsed from 1,254 PDFs, translated, and filtered by a five-minute web-search test (p.3, p.13). Each problem is annotated with a step-by-step solution in which every step names the theorem applied, the target quantity, the formula and the value; solutions average 8.1 steps, 15.6 for hard problems (pp.1-3). Models are scored at answer level (PSAS-A) and step level (PSAS-S): an LLM aligns each annotated step with the model's output and scores its formula and value, then the first error step is located and its type classified (pp.2, 4-6). 15 models are evaluated; the best, DeepSeek-R1, averages 56.75 at answer level and 73.26 at step level (p.7).
domain: high-school-exam and olympiad physics: classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetics, optics, relativity (pp.3-4)
size: 1,200 problems (300 per level) covering 147 theorems; PhysReason-mini subset of 200; 15 models (7 'non-O-like' and 8 'O-like' reasoning models) (pp.1-3, pp.6-7)
source_of_items: exams and competitions (Chinese Gaokao 2010-2024, Indian JEE Advanced 2010-2024, Chinese mock exams 2015-2024, IPhO 2008-2021, other olympiads; p.3, p.13)
has_gold_traces: yes: every problem has an annotated step-by-step solution, with per-step theorem, target, formula and value (Step Analysis) (pp.2-3, pp.14-15); solutions average 8.1 steps (p.1)
evaluation: step-level or process, LLM-based, plus answer level (DeepSeek-V3 as scorer, p.6): PSAS-A has an LLM extract each sub-question answer and check its semantic consistency with the gold answer, weighted by annotated solution length (p.4); PSAS-S has an LLM extract the model's content for each annotated step, scores formula and value (0.5 each) against the annotation, locates the first error step and classifies its type into seven categories (p.5). The framework rests on LLM information extraction and formula comparison (p.2, p.4).
human_validation: Translations checked by engineering PhD candidates with physics expertise (p.3, p.14). Annotation and evaluation were done by four graduate students from engineering disciplines who are co-authors (p.19). To validate the scorer, 1,000 of 8,400 model reasoning processes were manually annotated for answer correctness and the location of the first error step: PSAS with DeepSeek-V3 reached 99.35% answer accuracy and 98.04% first-error-step accuracy, against 87.81-93.31% and 33.18-37.54% for direct LLM evaluation (p.6, Table 2). No inter-annotator agreement is reported.
contamination_measures: search filter: problems whose solutions and answers can be found by a five-minute Google search are excluded, following GPQA (p.3, p.14); otherwise static items from public exams and olympiads (p.9 ethics statement)

engtrace_use.sentence: S-P1 (L172-177): 'While UGPhysics (Xu et al., 2025) and PhysReason (Zhang et al., 2025a) effectively test the application of reasoning to natural laws, others target advanced symbolic (Zhang et al., 2025b; Qiu et al., 2025) or qualitative (Wang et al., 2023; Shojaee et al., 2025) understanding.' S-P2 (L177-180, uncited, covers all six): 'Despite this progress, these benchmarks remain confined to theoretical physics, lacking the integrative context of engineering.'
engtrace_use.explanation: S-P1's characterisation is fair as far as it goes: PhysReason tests the application of physics theorems, and its annotations name the theorem behind every step (pp.2-3). But the May text omits what matters most for the comparison: PhysReason scores reasoning step by step against annotated gold steps (PSAS-S, p.5), locates the first erroneous step, and reports a human check of that scorer on 1,000 annotated reasoning processes (98.04% first-error-step accuracy, p.6). Read with the Introduction's 'no existing benchmark verifies this process' (L60-63) and the closing 'existing benchmarks remain limited to outcome matching' (L199-201), the paragraph implies PhysReason is outcome-only, which is the protocol's own example of a misleading use. S-P2's 'theoretical physics' is also loose: the problems are exam and olympiad physics (p.13), although the authors themselves say they test theorems 'under idealized conditions, rather than fully reflecting real-world physics scenarios' (p.9), which supports the engineering contrast.

suggested_wording: PhysReason (Zhang et al., 2025a) annotates 1,200 exam and olympiad physics problems with step-by-step solutions and scores model solutions step by step, using an LLM to align each model step with the annotated one and to compare its formula and value.
facts_to_cite: 1,200 problems: 25% knowledge-based, 75% reasoning-based in three difficulty levels; 81% include diagrams (p.1, p.4)
Sources are public college-entrance exams, mock exams and international olympiads (Gaokao, JEE Advanced, IPhO, among others) (p.3, p.13)
Every problem carries an annotated step-by-step solution; each step names the theorem, target quantity, formula and value; solutions average 8.1 steps and 15.6 for hard problems (pp.1-3)

Step-level scoring (PSAS-S): an LLM extracts the model's content for each annotated step, formula and value are each scored against the annotation (weight 0.5 each), and the first error step is located and classified (p.5)
The step-level scorer requires a one-to-one mapping between extracted and annotated steps (Algorithm 1, 'Assert |E| = |S|', p.5), so solutions are measured against one annotated path
On 1,000 manually annotated reasoning processes, PSAS located the first error step with 98.04% accuracy (DeepSeek-V3 scorer), against 33.18-37.54% for direct LLM evaluation (p.6)
Best model DeepSeek-R1: 56.75 answer-level, 73.26 step-level; its answer-level score falls from 75.11 on knowledge problems to 31.95 on hard problems (p.1, p.7)
Problems whose answers can be found in a five-minute web search are excluded (p.3)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares the most with EngTrace of any paper in this batch: gold step-level solutions; step-level, process-oriented evaluation with first-error localisation; a reported human check of the step scorer (pp.5-6). Lacks: generated instances (static public exam and olympiad problems, filtered by a search test); deterministic checks (both PSAS levels rely on LLM extraction and LLM comparison, p.2, pp.4-5); order-free intermediate targets (PSAS-S aligns to one annotated step sequence, p.5, whereas EngTrace's milestones are order-free values); an engineering domain (physics under idealised conditions, p.9); independent expert raters with agreement statistics (its annotators are four co-author graduate students, p.19, and no agreement figure is given). It has multimodal problems (81% with diagrams), which EngTrace does not.
notes: Consolidator must know: PhysReason directly contradicts the May claims that 'no existing benchmark verifies this process' (L60-63) and that 'existing benchmarks remain limited to outcome matching' (L199-201). The revised text must name it as the nearest physics precedent for step-level evaluation and say what EngTrace adds (generated instances from a private seed, deterministic answer and milestone checks with a residual judge, order-free milestones, engineering branches, expert raters with agreement statistics), not present step-level evaluation as new. Its scorer validation covers answer correctness and first-error-step location, not the per-step formula and value scores (p.6). Reference-list error (confirmed on p.1): printed 'Xinyi Zhang, Yuxuan Dong, Yutao Wu, Jiahui Huang, Chen Jia, Basura Fernando, Mike Zheng Shou, Li Zhang, and Jielin Liu'; the authors are Xinyu Zhang, Yuxuan Dong, Yanrui Wu, Jiaxing Huang, Chengyou Jia, Basura Fernando, Mike Zheng Shou, Lingling Zhang, Jun Liu.
